brief.headline: Memory spot intact: HBM sold-out through 2027, DRAM/NAND Q3 pricing +13-18%/+10-15% QoQ, hyperscaler capex tracking $660-690B in 2026
brief.summary: <cite index="8-3,8-13">Top three memory makers have pre-sold full HBM output for 2026, with Micron guiding 68% gross margin in Q2 2026.</cite> <cite index="11-1">TrendForce projects conventional DRAM contract prices rising 13-18% QoQ in Q3 2026 and NAND Flash 10-15% QoQ</cite>, following <cite index="15-7,15-8">Q2 jumps of 58-63% DRAM and 70-75% NAND</cite>. <cite index="19-5,19-6">Five hyperscalers (Amazon $200B, Alphabet $175-185B, Meta $115-135B, Microsoft $120B+, Oracle $50B) plan $660-690B capex in 2026</cite>, with <cite index="26-4">~75% allocated directly to AI infrastructure including GPUs, HBM servers, and networking</cite>. <cite index="29-2,29-11">TSMC's monthly CoWoS capacity targeting 120-140K wafers in 2026, with supply-demand gap narrowing from 20% to 10% by year-end</cite>.
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="9-3">SK Hynix controlled 57% of global HBM revenue in Q4 2025, versus Samsung 22% and Micron 21%</cite>. <cite index="5-3">UBS channel checks indicate SK Hynix will likely secure ~50% HBM market share in 2026</cite>. <cite index="5-4">Pricing pushback possible as Samsung inches closer to HBM3E qualification</cite>, but <cite index="5-7">Hynix expects only minimal to modest downtick for 2026 versus 2025</cite>. <cite index="8-8,8-9">SK Hynix positioned as primary beneficiary, claiming only supplier able to deliver both HBM3E and next-gen HBM4 at scale</cite>. Long SK Hynix vs Samsung on HBM3E qual timing delta and existing Nvidia design-in advantage; watch Samsung's HBM4 roadmap as potential catch-up catalyst H2 2027.

memory_cycle.stage: Mid-to-late upcycle, pricing power intact but deceleration visible
memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="11-1">Q3 2026 DRAM contract price growth of 13-18% QoQ and NAND 10-15% represents marked slowdown</cite> from <cite index="15-7,15-8">Q2's record 58-63% DRAM and 70-75% NAND QoQ increases</cite>. <cite index="8-5,8-7">Chipmakers prioritizing HBM for AI infrastructure, tightening mainstream DRAM/NAND availability; every wafer to HBM denies LPDDR5X/SSD supply</cite>. <cite index="9-1,9-2">Memory shortages expected through 2027, giving suppliers stronger pricing power than historically enjoyed</cite>. <cite index="11-9,11-10">AI inference and hyperscale demand keeps supply constrained; less capacity for consumer memory prevents price declines even as PC/smartphone demand weakens</cite>. Conventional DRAM peak ASPs likely Q3/Q4 2026; HBM pricing power extends into 2028.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="5-6">HBM bit shipments projected to jump 35% in 2026 to 17.1 billion gigabits</cite>. <cite index="8-2,8-3">HBM3E expected to remain dominant AI memory through 2026, with pricing power intact until new capacity arrives post-2027; top three memory makers allocated full HBM output with Micron at 68% gross margin Q2 2026</cite>. <cite index="9-4">SK Hynix reported five-fold quarterly profit jump in April, stating HBM demand expected to exceed supply over next three years</cite>. <cite index="1-5">Micron integrating HBM3E 36GB 12-high into AMD Instinct MI350 Series</cite>. Nvidia controls <cite index="30-4,30-5">~60% of 2026 CoWoS capacity, booking 595K wafers total with 515K from TSMC (510K CoWoS-L) for Rubin, Vera, GB100</cite>. Supply remains binary constraint on AI accelerator shipments through H1 2027.

news_pulse.headline: July DRAM DDR4 8Gb at $24, up 14.3% MoM; NAND 128Gb MLC $30.1, up 4.3% MoM—19 consecutive months of NAND increases
news_pulse.implication: Spot pricing confirms TrendForce contract forecasts; AI-driven capacity diversion sustaining pricing power despite consumer demand softness

news_pulse.headline: ADATA warns DRAM contract prices +20-30% Q3 2026, NAND +35-40%; shortages expected until 2028
news_pulse.implication: Module maker passing through upstream price pressure; validates sustained HBM reallocation squeezing consumer memory availability

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 capex now $660-690B (Amazon $200B, Alphabet $175-185B, Meta $115-135B, MSFT $120B+, Oracle $50B)
news_pulse.implication: Aggregate spend nearly doubles 2025; confirms demand-side support for memory pricing through 2027 despite rising ROI scrutiny

news_pulse.headline: Goldman Sachs raises four hyperscaler cumulative capex 2025-2030 to $5.3T from $4.5T pre-Q1 earnings
news_pulse.implication: Upward revisions to multi-year capex support extended HBM demand visibility; 2026 alone tracks $725B, up 77% YoY

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS capacity targeting 120-140K wpm end-2026, supply-demand gap narrowing from 20% to 10% by year-end
news_pulse.implication: CoWoS bottleneck easing but still 10% undersupplied; validates TSMC's 80%+ CAGR 2022-2027 for advanced packaging capacity

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix 57% HBM revenue share Q4 2025 vs Samsung 22%, Micron 21%; UBS expects Hynix ~50% share in 2026
news_pulse.implication: Hynix maintains leadership but share compression likely as Samsung HBM3E qual nears; watch Nvidia supplier diversification efforts

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix YTD stock gains +114%, +186% respectively as of May 2026; investor warnings on cyclicality resurfacing
news_pulse.implication: Valuation stretch acknowledged; market pricing structural shift away from boom-bust, but Deutsche Bank flags TurboQuant risk to AI memory demand

news_pulse.headline: Bank of America forecasts global DRAM revenue +51% in 2026, NAND +45%, with ASPs up 30%+
news_pulse.implication: Revenue growth driven by price, not volume to consumer markets; PC/smartphone DRAM/NAND volumes shrinking as HBM reallocation intensifies

Implied vol likely elevated into any Samsung HBM3E qualification headlines or Nvidia supplier allocation updates.
